# Security and Privacy Checklist: PB Store on the Reader

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for the signature and the serial memory, rollback protection, trust anchors and a wrong reader clock, the absence of overrides in the release build, the redacted log, Wi-Fi handling, no network at start-up, path and `view.json` checks, and consistency with the installer's rules are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md, constitution 2.1.0 Principles III, IV, V and VII, and what feature 002 decided: its spec FR-006 to FR-008, FR-031, FR-034 to FR-036, `docs/security-review.md` rows I1 to I22, `docs/installer-rules.md`). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]`. The installer's own checklist (`specs/002-pb-installer-linux/checklists/security.md`) is not repeated; this list asks what changes when the same rules run on the reader. Safety and recovery items are in `install-safety.md`.

## Signature, Serial Memory and Rollback Protection

- [ ] CHK001 Is the behavior defined when the remembered serial, or the cached catalog it belongs to, is missing, unreadable or damaged (first run, a deleted `system/pbstore/app/`, a damaged file): accept any verified catalog and say so, as the installer does, or refuse? [Gap, Spec §FR-003; compare 002 §FR-007, row I2]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the reason for keeping the serial on the reader written down, given that feature 002 deliberately keeps it on the computer "so that a different reader cannot reset it" and the reader's storage can be changed or cleared from any computer? Is the weaker protection (a reset by deleting the folder) stated as an accepted risk? [Consistency, Assumption, Spec §Clarifications "serial on the reader"; 002 Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it stated whether the cached catalog and the remembered serial are one record or two, which of them decides when they disagree, and what happens when power is lost between writing the new catalog and the new serial? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec say that the reader's clock plays no part in the signature check, the serial comparison or the offer rule (only in the certificate check), so that a wrong clock cannot weaken rollback protection? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the rule for an *equal* serial with *different bytes* stated for the store, or accepted as a residual risk as in the installer (row I4)? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases "older than the last accepted"; 002 row I4]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the list of built-in public keys specified as in feature 002 (a short list, normally two, never more than three, changed only by a reviewed change), instead of only "the keys built into the store"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002; constitution Principle III; 002 §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK007 Is it stated that the signature is checked before *any* interpretation of the catalog on every load, including the first screen after start-up, and that nothing from a catalog that failed the check is shown, stored or used for the list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003, §Story 1 scenario 6]

## Trust Anchors, TLS and the Reader's Clock

- [ ] CHK008 Is "the device's own store when it is usable" defined for the reader (what makes it usable, where it is, what happens if it holds an old bundle), and is the location of that store an unverified device fact with a manual task? [Clarity, Assumption, Spec §FR-004; constitution Tech Stack "unverified"]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the age of the bundled CA file addressed (how it is refreshed, and what the user sees when certificates of the host change faster than the store is updated)? [Gap, Spec §FR-004; compare 002 row "embedded CA bundle ages"]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the decision against a custom CA file reflected in what the user is told when a network intercepts HTTPS (the message names the certificate and says no setting can accept it), so that no message suggests a workaround? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005, §Assumptions "networks that intercept HTTPS"]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the transport failures given distinct plain messages as in feature 002 (host unreachable, invalid or expired certificate, wrong host name, wrong clock), or only the wrong clock and a generic certificate message? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases "clock", §FR-005; 002 §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the test for a "clearly wrong" clock defined (a build-time release date, a floor, or the certificate's own dates), including a clock far in the future, and is it stated that the guess changes only the wording of the message and never the check itself? [Ambiguity, Spec §Edge Cases "clock"]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the limits of feature 002 restated or referenced for the reader: HTTPS-only redirects, at most five, a size limit per download (the signed `package_size` for a package, 1 MiB for the catalog), a total time limit? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-006; 002 §FR-006]

## No Override in the Release Build

- [ ] CHK014 Does FR-007 cover files as well as options and environment variables, given that `system/pbstore/app/` can be edited from any computer: is it stated that no file there (settings, cache, a stray config) can change the catalog address, the keys or the trust anchors? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-041]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the separate test build required to be unmistakable from the release (a different name, menu entry id and state folder), so that it can never be installed or updated over the released store by mistake? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK016 Is there a requirement and a success criterion that the released device program is inspected for test-only strings and for the right key list, like the installer's inspection of its release file? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §FR-007, §SC-006; 002 rows I6 and `test_release_binary`]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the installer's source-level rules (test names only under the test-build switch, no `system(` or `popen(`, no hard-coded SDK path) required to apply to the store's sources as well, or is the extension left to the plan? [Consistency, Dependency, Spec §FR-014; constitution Development Workflow "Reviewers MUST reject"]

## Network Contact, Wi-Fi Handling and Start-up

- [ ] CHK018 Is "network contact" defined for the zero-connection rule (a DNS lookup, a connection attempt, a captive-portal or time check, scanning for networks), and does it include the launcher and a self-update swap at start-up? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §SC-004, §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK019 Are icons covered: the catalog entry has an `icon_url`, so is it stated that the store fetches no icon at list time or at start-up (or fetches it only during a user-started action), and that links from the catalog are shown as text and opened only by a user action and only if HTTPS? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-011; 002 §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the Wi-Fi handling specified when the reader has no saved network, when the user must pick a network on the reader's own screen, and that the store never asks for, reads or keeps a network name or password? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, §FR-039]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the rule "switch it off again only if the store switched it on" complete for the case where the earlier Wi-Fi state cannot be read, where the user changes it during the action, and where the store is ended by the reader before it can switch it off? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-001, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the content of a request limited as in feature 002 (no identifier, no machine or user detail, beyond what HTTPS inevitably contains plus the program's name and version), and is that consistent with constitution Principle V, which allows only "what an HTTPS request inevitably contains"? [Conflict, Spec §FR-001; constitution Principle V; 002 §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the user told which hosts the store contacts (the catalog host and the host the package comes from, which redirects to others), as Principle VIII asks for apps' origin, in About or in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-037, §FR-015; constitution Principle VIII]

## Redacted Log and Personal Data

- [ ] CHK024 Is the list of personal data complete for a reader: besides the Wi-Fi name, password, serial number, e-mail address and user name, does it include the network address, the hardware address, the reader's name, an account name, and any text a network library puts into an error string? [Completeness, Spec §FR-039, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the rule "readable by the user only" of feature 002 replaced by something achievable, since the log sits on the reader's FAT storage where every computer that mounts it can read it, and is it stated why a log without personal data is acceptable there? [Conflict, Spec §FR-039; 002 §FR-031]
- [ ] CHK026 Is it specified what the log screen may show (the last N entries, the same redaction as the file) and whether a copy of the log can leave the reader other than by mounting it? [Gap, Spec §FR-039, §Story 8]
- [ ] CHK027 Are untrusted texts (names, descriptions, file names from catalog and package) required to be shown as plain text with control and direction-changing characters neutralised, and bounded in length, on every screen and in the log, as the installer does for terminals and pages? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-011; 002 §FR-035, row I11]
- [ ] CHK028 Is a bound set for the log's growth together with the cache and the other state in `system/pbstore/app/`, so that the store cannot fill the storage it also needs for staging? [Gap, Spec §FR-039, §FR-041]

## Package Integrity, Paths and `view.json`

- [ ] CHK029 Is the bytes-written-are-the-bytes-verified rule of feature 002 (verified once and kept) restated for the reader, where FR-015 puts the download into the store's own area on the FAT volume and reads it again; is the interval between verification and use bounded against change? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015; 002 §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the order of checks fixed and consistent with feature 002 (size, SHA-256 against the signed entry, then ZIP and manifest rules, nothing parsed before the hash matched), or only "every check of feature 002"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015; 002 §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the root of all writes defined for the device (a fixed place chosen by the store, not a user choice), together with the rule that nothing outside the paths of the reader-layout contract is written, and is the reader-layout contract named as the source for `system/pbstore/app/`? [Gap, Dependency, Spec §FR-040; 002 §FR-035]
- [ ] CHK032 Does the spec address that the reader's desktop is running and may read or write `view.json` while the store checks its shape and edits it, and that the "reader changed since the plan" check (`E-INS-25`) applies? [Gap, Spec §FR-015, §FR-040; 002 row I15]
- [ ] CHK033 Are the rules for hostile package paths (traversal, absolute paths, case-only differences, files owned by another app, reserved data folder names, `pbstore`) stated by reference with their rule ids, so that "writes outside the allowed folders" in the edge cases and `E-INS-19` agree? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases "outside the allowed folders", §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the shape check of `view.json` stated for the store as a refusal with a message and no repair, including that the store never creates a missing group and never rewrites a file it cannot parse, and that the backup is made before the edit? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases "desktop configuration", §FR-040]

## Self-Update and Adoption Trust

- [ ] CHK035 Is the integrity of a prepared self-update at the swap anchored to something the maintainer signed (the catalog entry) and not only to a hash record written on the same writable storage? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK036 Is a threat model stated for the reader (someone who mounts the storage on a computer can change any file, the launcher included), with what is in scope (network attackers, hostile packages, a hostile catalog) and what is not (an attacker with the unlocked storage)? [Gap, Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 Is it stated whether the store tells the user when the version it runs, or an installed app, has been withdrawn (a security reason to update), while keeping the rule that nothing is changed because of a withdrawal? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]

## Consistency with the Installer's Rules and Traceability

- [ ] CHK038 Is there a mapping from the rules the store inherits (rule ids `E-INS-nn`, `E-CAT-nn`, `E-PKG-nn`) to the store's behavior, listing which ids cannot occur on the reader (for example `E-INS-01` to `E-INS-06`, which are about finding a drive), so that the same id never carries two meanings? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases intro, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK039 Do the success criteria cover each security requirement of the request with a measurable case: rollback, an invalid signature, a wrong clock, the absence of overrides in the release program, a redacted log, and no network at start-up (only SC-004, SC-006 and SC-010 are close)? [Coverage, Measurability, Spec §SC-004, §SC-006, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK040 Are the new rules for the reader (Principle IV's self-update bullet, Principle V's Wi-Fi bullet, Principle VII's shared contracts) each traceable to a requirement and a success criterion in the spec? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001, §FR-032 to §FR-036, §FR-041, §SC-012; constitution 2.1.0]

## Notes
